PREVIOUS NOTE: STAGED, NOT APPLIED — Security review REQUIRED (it changes who can read an identity column on a public table and adds a client-callable read of a cross-player surface). Closes the NAMED PRE-LAUNCH P2 (Security, 2026-09-13; PRIORITY_BOARD §10 and the header of 2026-09-13-town-presence.sql, which filed it as a door it could only defend in depth): 2026-09-08-hearthfind.sql granted SELECT on ALL of world_finds — user_id and slot included — to anon AND authenticated, and profiles/display_names are public-read, so any client joined them and named every finder INCLUDING characters who set presence_quiet. The shipped client did exactly that (src/features/hearthfind.js:964 selected user_id off the board, :950 resolved it through display_names into the global chat line), which is why hr_town_refresh's crier quiet filter "buys nothing today" by its own admission. THE FIX: hr_world_finds_of(p_limit int default 50) — a STABLE SECURITY DEFINER inner behind a VOLATILE gated wrapper (the hr_town_of shape, because the rate gate is an UPSERT and Postgres refuses a write inside STABLE) — returns the newest ≤200 board rows through a LITERAL 8-key allowlist (id, name, item_id, source_kind, source_id, one_in, found_at, nth) with the finder's DISPLAY NAME already minted server-side from the same authority hr_town_refresh's crier uses (coalesce(profiles.display_name,'Adventurer')), NULL for a presence_quiet finder, and NO user_id and NO slot; then the table's client SELECT is narrowed so the de-anonymising join has no left-hand side. ⚠ THE REVOKE IS `revoke select on world_finds from anon, authenticated` FOLLOWED BY `grant select (id,item_id,source_kind,source_id,one_in,found_at)` — NOT `revoke select (user_id)`: PostgreSQL will not let a column-level REVOKE carve an exception out of a table-level grant (the revoke finds no column grant to remove and silently no-ops), so the literal form in the brief would have left the file decorative. §6(d) proves the result with has_column_privilege per role per column, from BOTH sides (identity gone AND every anonymous column still readable AND no write privilege created), and the node guard adds THREE executed statements under `set role authenticated` that must each raise 42501 — the column in the target list, in a WHERE clause and in ORDER BY. The WHERE form is the one Security's review named as the real attack: a MEMBERSHIP ORACLE returns no user_id at all and still answers "does this account hold a rare find?" about a uuid taken from any public roster, so a revoke covering only the target list would leave presence_quiet hollow while every projection assertion stayed green. QUIET NULLS THE NAME, IT DOES NOT DROP THE ROW — deliberately DIFFERENT from the crier, which drops it: the board is where "the 3rd ever found in Hearthrise" comes from, and deleting rows would let one player's privacy setting silently corrupt every later ordinal for everybody. It also closes the ordinal handoff filed at src/features/hearthfind.js:40 and a latent client bug: that read was order=id.asc&limit=500, i.e. the OLDEST five hundred rows, which freezes the board (no new find ever in the window, so no chat line and no moving count) once the table passes 500 — hr_world_finds_prune keeps 20000. `nth` is now a real server-side ordinal over the table, served by the new world_finds_item_idx (item_id, id); still a lower bound after a prune and still suppressed by the 30 s broadcast clamp, so the client's honest-or-absent contract is unchanged. READERS ENUMERATED BEFORE REVOKING (src/**, supabase/functions/**, supabase/migrations/**): the client board poll (moved to the RPC) and namesFor/display_names (deleted) are the only client readers; hr_apply's clamp+insert, hr_world_finds_prune and hr_town_refresh's crier are all SECURITY DEFINER owner-side and unaffected; the Edge never touches the board; and world_finds has no Realtime publication membership (2026-09-06-realtime-publication-trim.sql) so no Postgres-Changes subscription can break. Grants: EXECUTE to authenticated ONLY (the inner owner-only, anon excluded — the board line is injected into the global chat dock, which a signed-out visitor does not have, so the client half gates the poll on a session); one hr_rpc_gate bucket at 6/min (the poll is 0.67/min). ⚠ hr_rpc_gate is a FULL RESTATEMENT here, not the usual anchored patch: `node tests/patch-chain-guard.mjs` went PATCH-3 red on the anchored form (its chain was already 2 deep behind 2026-09-13-town-presence.sql and an ack would have needed that APPLIED file edited too), and the guard's rule is right.
